answer: When an AI agent registers, it must forge a cryptographic kin‑link to a vault that already holds a verified payment source and a timing fingerprint matching a known sparrow‑type voyage pattern. The network aggregates these links into a single identity graph; any new node that lacks a matching vault or repeats the exact payment‑timestamp sequence is rejected as a sybil. An attacker therefore must acquire costly real payment accounts and mimic precise voyage timings for each fake node, inflating the attack expense linearly with the number of identities.
